item.title: Beach, Coast, Shore
item.description: VOA Learning English - Beach, Coast, Shore. This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Doyeon in Korea about the usage of three similar words. Here is the question: Hello. I want to know the differences between the beach, . . . c... English original and Chinese translation in full notes.
item.content:encoded:
English & 中文

This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Doyeon in Korea about the usage of three similar words.
本周的《名师答疑》中，我们回答来自韩国Doyeon关于三个相似单词用法的问题。

Here is the question:
问题是：

Hello.
你好。

I want to know the differences between
我想知道它们之间的区别

the beach, . . . coast and shore.
海滩、海岸和滨岸。

Thank you.
谢谢。

You ask a useful question, Doyeon. Beach, shore and coast are related words, but they have some important differences.
你的问题很有用，Doyeon。Beach、shore和coast是相关词汇，但有一些重要区别。

Beach
Beach（海滩）

The word "beach" is the most specific of the three words.
“Beach”是这三个词中最具体的。

The Collins online dictionary defines beach as "a nearly level stretch of pebbles and sand beside a sea, lake, etc., often washed by high water."
柯林斯在线词典将beach定义为“海、湖等旁边近乎平坦的卵石和沙地带，常被高潮淹没。”

Ocean beaches are popular places to visit.
海洋海滩是受欢迎的旅游景点。

We often use the phrase "at the beach" to express the idea of spending time in the general area of the beach, as in the following example:
我们常用“at the beach”表示在海滩周边区域度过时光，例如：

They will vacation at the beach this summer.
他们今年夏天将在海滩度假。

We usually say "on the beach" when describing specific activities we do there:
描述在海滩上的具体活动时，我们通常用“on the beach”：

She went for a walk on the beach.
她在海滩上散步。

I'm going to spend my afternoon on the beach.
我打算下午待在海滩上。

They are playing football on the beach.
他们正在海滩上踢足球。

Coast
Coast（海岸）

The Learning English Word Book defines coast as "land on the edge of the ocean."
《学英语词汇手册》将coast定义为“海洋边缘的陆地。”

We can use the word to describe a wide area, however.
不过，这个词也可以用来描述广阔的区域。

For example, Baltimore, Maryland is an East Coast city even though it is several kilometers from the Atlantic Ocean.
例如，马里兰州巴尔的摩是东海岸城市，尽管它距离大西洋约几公里。

Here are more examples of how we can use "coast" in a sentence.
以下是更多使用“coast”的例句：

The Florida coast has many nice towns and beaches.
佛罗里达海岸有许多美丽的小镇和海滩。

The coast of California extends over 1,300 kilometers.
加利福尼亚海岸线绵延超过1300公里。

Like the expression "at the beach," we can say "on the coast" when describing the general area, as in the following example:
与“at the beach”类似，我们可以用“on the coast”来描述一般区域，例如：

Her mother has lived on the coast for 30 years.
她母亲住在海边已有30年。

We can use the expression "off the coast of" to describe an area of ocean or sea relative to a place on land:
我们可以用“off the coast of”来描述相对于陆地的海域：

The island is about 60 kilometers off the coast of Africa.
该岛距离非洲海岸约60公里。

Shore
Shore（滨岸/岸）

The Merriam-Webster online dictionary defines the word "shore" as "the land bordering a usually large body of water."
韦氏在线词典将“shore”定义为“通常濒临大面积水域的陆地。”

Shore can sometimes mean the beach, but not always.
Shore有时可以指海滩，但并非总是如此。

For example, you might swim to shore and come out of the water onto a beach.
例如，你可以游到岸边，然后从水里走上沙滩。

item.title: Sew and Knit
item.description: VOA Learning English - Sew and Knit. This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Rohullah in Afghanistan about using the words "sew" and "knit" and related terms. Dear VOA Learning English, I am sending this email to know wha... English original and Chinese translation in full notes.
item.content:encoded:
English & 中文

This week on Ask a Teacher, we answer a question from Rohullah in Afghanistan about using the words "sew" and "knit" and related terms.
本周在《问老师》节目中，我们回答来自阿富汗的Rohullah提出的关于使用“缝”和“织”及相关词汇的问题。

Dear VOA Learning English,
亲爱的VOA学英语：

I am sending this email to know what the differences are between "sewing and knitting" or "sew and knit."
我发这封邮件是想知道“缝纫和编织”或“缝和织”之间的区别。

Besides [that], I wanted to know what I can call a woman or a man that makes clothes.
除此之外，我还想知道可以怎么称呼做衣服的男人或女人。

Thank you
谢谢。

I'm happy to answer this question, Rohullah.
Rohullah，我很高兴回答这个问题。

An important difference between sewing and knitting is that when we sew, we connect pieces of fabric or cloth that are already made.
缝纫和编织的一个重要区别是，当我们缝纫时，我们连接已经做好的布料或织物片。

When we knit, we make the cloth itself from strings called yarn.
当我们编织时，我们用叫做纱线的线来制作布料本身。

Also, the word "sewing" can describe many ways people connect or repair fabric and clothes.
此外，“缝纫”这个词可以描述人们连接或修补布料和衣服的多种方式。

For example, people can sew many kinds of clothes, such as socks, shirts, dresses, hats, and gloves.
例如，人们可以缝制多种衣服，如袜子、衬衫、连衣裙、帽子和手套。

People can also sew larger things, such as window coverings or tents.
人们还可以缝制更大的物品，如窗帘或帐篷。

A person can sew using a sewing machine or simply by using their hands with a needle and thread.
一个人可以用缝纫机缝纫，也可以只用针线手工缝纫。

Knitting does not generally require use of a machine or a needle and thread.
编织通常不需要使用机器或针线。

To knit, a person uses thicker strings called yarn, along with two thin sticks called knitting needles.
编织时，人们使用较粗的线（称为纱线），以及两根细棒（称为织针）。

Yarn is usually made of small, natural pieces, called fibers, such as wool or cotton.
纱线通常由细小的天然纤维制成，如羊毛或棉花。

While sewing thread is often less than one millimeter thick, knitting yarn is generally two to five millimeters thick.
缝纫线通常不到一毫米粗，而编织纱线通常有两到五毫米粗。

Many people who knit make clothing for cold weather, such as wool sweaters, hats, and scarves.
许多编织者制作寒冷天气穿的衣服，如羊毛衫、帽子和围巾。

They may also knit blankets or other things that can be used in the home.
他们也可能编织毯子或其他家中可用的物品。

More than 50 years ago, most Americans who earned money sewing clothes in a factory were women. They were called "seamstresses."
五十多年前，大多数在工厂靠缝制衣服赚钱的美国人都是女性。她们被称为“女裁缝”。

Today, we sometimes call any person who sews a "sewist."
今天，我们有时称任何缝纫的人为“缝纫者”。

Or we can simply say "a person who sews."
或者我们可以简单地说“一个缝纫的人”。

And a person whose job is to sew or repair clothes to make them fit well is called a tailor.
而一个以缝制或修补衣服使其合身为职业的人被称为裁缝。

For our readers and listeners, what are your questions about American English?
对于我们的读者和听众，你们对美国英语有什么问题吗？

Do you like to knit or sew?
你喜欢编织还是缝纫？

We want to hear from you! Send us an email at learningenglish@voanews.com.
我们想听到你的声音！请给我们发邮件至learningenglish@voanews.com。

And please let us know where you are from, too.
也请告诉我们你来自哪里。

And that's Ask a Teacher.
这就是《问老师》节目。

I'm Andrew Smith.
我是安德鲁·史密斯。

Source: VOA Learning English

Read full transcript →

item.title: How Physical Therapists Can Prevent Future Health Problems
item.description: VOA Learning English - How Physical Therapists Can Prevent Future Health Problems. Many of us might only seek out physical therapists if we are recovering from accidental injuries or surgery. However, medical experts say these specialists can also help prevent many health problems ... English original and Chinese translation in full notes.
item.content:encoded:
English & 中文

Many of us might only seek out physical therapists if we are recovering from accidental injuries or surgery.
我们很多人可能只有在从意外受伤或手术中恢复时才会寻求物理治疗师。

However, medical experts say these specialists can also help prevent many health problems if they are seen on a regular basis.
然而，医学专家表示，如果定期就诊，这些专家也能帮助预防许多健康问题。

One leader in the industry, Sharon Dunn, even calls physical therapists "the best-kept secret in health care."
该行业的一位领导者Sharon Dunn甚至称物理治疗师是“医疗保健领域最保守的秘密”。

Dunn is the past president of the American Physical Therapy Association (APTA).
Dunn是美国物理治疗协会（APTA）的前任主席。

She recently told The Associated Press she thinks people need to look at physical therapists in a new way - as health practitioners who can help identify possible medical issues before they appear.
她最近告诉美联社，她认为人们需要以新的眼光看待物理治疗师——作为能够帮助在疾病出现前识别潜在健康问题的医疗从业者。

Other health experts share this opinion.
其他健康专家也持相同观点。

They include Roger Herr, the current president of the APTA, and Gammon Earhart of Washington University in St. Louis.
其中包括APTA现任主席Roger Herr和圣路易斯华盛顿大学的Gammon Earhart。

They both shared Dunn's prevention message in separate discussions with the AP.
两人在与美联社的单独讨论中都分享了Dunn的预防理念。

Earhart urges people to think about physical therapists just as they do dentists.
Earhart敦促人们像对待牙医一样看待物理治疗师。

"Even if you're not having any problem, you go in and have everything checked out."
“即使你没有任何问题，也要去检查一下所有方面。”

She noted that such examinations could help find and deal with problems early.
她指出，这样的检查有助于及早发现和处理问题。

For example, an exam could include a patient's health history and current health - things like physical activity, sleep, nutrition, and so on.
例如，检查可以包括患者的健康史和当前健康状况，如身体活动、睡眠、营养等。

This could be followed by a look at how a person is moving.
随后可以观察一个人的运动方式。

Exams might uncover things like postural issues or unusual body movements.
检查可能会发现诸如姿势问题或异常身体动作等问题。

Herr is a big supporter of yearly wellness visits.
Herr是年度健康检查的坚定支持者。

He told the AP he believes physical therapists can be helpful for all kinds of people - the young, athletes, or anyone who wants to be as "independent as possible."
他告诉美联社，他相信物理治疗师对各类人群都有帮助——年轻人、运动员，或者任何希望“尽可能独立”的人。

In the United States, you can now visit a physical therapist in all 50 states without needing permission from a doctor or surgeon.
在美国，你现在可以在所有50个州直接看物理治疗师，无需医生或外科医生的许可。

However, a yearly exam might not be covered by a person's health insurance.
然而，年度检查可能不在个人的医疗保险覆盖范围内。

This could prevent some from seeking out care.
这可能会阻止一些人寻求护理。

Earhart estimated such a visit in areas across the U.S. Midwest might cost around $150.
Earhart估计，在美国中西部地区的这样一次就诊费用大约为150美元。

Herr suggested a cost of $200-$300 in more costly areas.
Herr建议在费用更高的地区，费用为200-300美元。

But both experts said that in the long run, such exams might save money and can add healthy years.
但两位专家都表示，从长远来看，这样的检查可能节省费用，并增加健康的寿命。

"I think if people understood more that the way they move might be setting them up for a problem down the line, they'd be much more inclined to see a physical therapist," Earhart said.
Earhart说：“我认为如果人们更了解他们的运动方式可能会在将来导致问题，他们会更愿意去看物理治疗师。”

item.title: Methods for Protecting Earth against an Asteroid Strike
item.description: VOA Learning English - Methods for Protecting Earth against an Asteroid Strike. Astronomers following asteroid activity in space estimate there is a very small chance an object large enough to destroy a whole city could strike Earth in 2032. But space agency officials say even i... English original and Chinese translation in full notes.
item.content:encoded:
English & 中文

Astronomers following asteroid activity in space estimate there is a very small chance an object large enough to destroy a whole city could strike Earth in 2032.
跟踪太空中小行星活动的天文学家估计，一个足以摧毁整座城市的物体在2032年撞击地球的可能性非常小。

But space agency officials say even if such an asteroid keeps heading on a path toward Earth, the world is now much better-equipped to defend itself against such a threat.
但航天局官员表示，即使这样的小行星继续沿着朝向地球的路径前进，世界现在也更有能力防御此类威胁。

The American space agency NASA recently estimated there was a 3.1 percent chance that asteroid 2024 YR4 would hit Earth on December 22, 2032.
美国航天局NASA最近估计，小行星2024 YR4在2032年12月22日撞击地球的可能性为3.1%。

That is the highest probability predicted for such a large space rock in modern times.
这是现代对如此大的太空岩石预测的最高概率。

Richard Moissl is head of the European Space Agency's (ESA) planetary defense office.
理查德·莫伊塞尔是欧洲航天局（ESA）行星防御办公室的负责人。

While recognizing the risk the asteroid could present, he told the French news agency AFP people should not panic over such predictions.
在承认小行星可能带来的风险的同时，他告诉法国新闻机构法新社，人们不应因这类预测而恐慌。

Astronomers have noted that the more data they gather, the odds of a direct asteroid hit are expected to keep rising over time.
天文学家指出，他们收集的数据越多，小行星直接撞击的几率预计会随时间持续上升。

However, scientists say at a certain point the odds will likely drop down to zero.
然而，科学家表示，在某个节点，几率可能会降至零。

Moissl said he thinks it is important to remember that even in the unlikely event the probability keeps rising to 100 percent, the world is "not defenseless."
莫伊塞尔说，他认为重要的是要记住，即使在不太可能的情况下概率持续上升至100%，世界也“并非毫无防御能力”。

Here are some methods currently being considered as defensive measures to keep humanity safe in case there is a real threat.
以下是一些目前正在考虑的防御措施，以在出现真实威胁时确保人类安全。

Only one planetary defense method has been tried against an asteroid.
只有一种行星防御方法曾在小行星上尝试过。

In 2022, NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) sent a spacecraft into the 160-meter-wide Dimorphos asteroid.
2022年，NASA的双小行星重定向测试（DART）将一艘航天器送入宽160米的迪莫弗斯小行星。

The effort successfully changed the asteroid's orbit around a larger space rock.
这次行动成功改变了该小行星围绕一颗更大太空岩石的轨道。

Bruce Betts is chief scientist for the nonprofit Planetary Society.
布鲁斯·贝茨是非营利组织行星学会的首席科学家。

He told AFP that space agencies could hit the 2024 YR4 asteroid with several spacecrafts, observing how each one changed the path.
他告诉法新社，航天机构可以用多艘航天器撞击2024 YR4小行星，观察每一艘如何改变其路径。

The asteroid discovered in December is estimated to be 40-90 meters wide -- about half the size of Dimorphos.
去年12月发现的这颗小行星估计宽40-90米，大约是迪莫弗斯大小的一半。

"You have to take care not to overdo it," Moissl warned.
“必须小心不要过度，”莫伊塞尔警告说。

He said this is because if a spacecraft only partly destroys an asteroid, it could send smaller pieces of the space rock heading toward Earth.
他说，这是因为如果航天器只部分摧毁小行星，可能会将更小的碎片推向地球。

A separate idea would involve sending a large spacecraft to fly alongside a threatening asteroid.
另一个想法涉及发射一艘大型航天器与有威胁的小行星并排飞行。

The spacecraft would not touch the asteroid, but would use its gravitational force to pull it away from Earth.
航天器不会接触小行星，而是利用其引力将其拉离地球。

item.title: Total Lunar Eclipse to Turn Moon Red
item.description: VOA Learning English - Total Lunar Eclipse to Turn Moon Red. A total lunar eclipse is about to make the moon appear a reddish color across the Western Hemisphere. The event will happen Thursday night into Friday morning. The best places to see the eclipse wil... English original and Chinese translation in full notes.
item.content:encoded:
English & 中文

A total lunar eclipse is about to make the moon appear a reddish color across the Western Hemisphere.
一场月全食即将使西半球的月亮呈现红色。

The event will happen Thursday night into Friday morning.
这一事件将在周四晚至周五早上发生。

The best places to see the eclipse will be in North America and South America.
观赏月食的最佳地点将是北美洲和南美洲。

Parts of Africa and Europe may also get brief views.
非洲和欧洲部分地区也可能短暂看到。

A lunar eclipse happens when the sun, Earth, and moon line up just right, with Earth positioned between the sun and moon.
当太阳、地球和月球完美排列，地球位于太阳和月球之间时，就会发生月食。

This causes the Earth to create a shadow on the moon.
这导致地球在月球上投下阴影。

In a total lunar eclipse, the Earth's shadow covers all of the moon.
在月全食中，地球的阴影覆盖了整个月球。

Another kind of eclipse is a solar eclipse.
另一种食是日食。

In a solar eclipse, the moon gets in a position where it blocks light from the sun, causing a partial or full shadow on Earth.
在日食中，月球处于阻挡太阳光的位置，导致地球出现部分或全部阴影。

A total lunar eclipse can also be called a blood moon.
月全食也可以被称为血月。

It makes the moon appear reddish-orange, similar to the element copper.
它使月亮呈现红橙色，类似于铜元素。

The color comes from small amounts of sunlight passing through the Earth's atmosphere.
这种颜色来自于少量阳光穿过地球大气层。

The American space agency NASA says lunar and solar eclipses happen between four and seven times a year.
美国航天局NASA表示，月食和日食每年发生四到七次。

The last total lunar eclipse was in 2022.
上一次月全食发生在2022年。

This one will be visible for about one hour starting Friday morning at 2:26 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).
这次月全食将在周五凌晨2点26分（美国东部夏令时间）开始，持续约一小时。

The time when the Earth's shadow covers all of the moon will be close to 3 a.m. EDT.
地球阴影完全覆盖月球的时刻将接近美国东部夏令时间凌晨3点。

"As long as the sky is clear, you should be able to see it," Shannon Schmoll told the Associated Press.
“只要天空晴朗，你应该能看到它，”香农·施莫尔告诉美联社。

She is the director of Abrams Planetarium at Michigan State University.
她是密歇根州立大学艾布拉姆斯天文馆的馆长。

No special equipment will be needed to see the reddish moon.
观看红色的月亮不需要特殊设备。

The total lunar eclipse may be harder to see in Europe and Africa because the moon will be close to setting.
由于月亮即将落下，欧洲和非洲可能更难看到月全食。

Michael Faison is an astronomy expert from Yale University.
迈克尔·费森是耶鲁大学的天文学专家。

He told the AP, "This is really an eclipse for North and South America."
他告诉美联社：“这确实是北美洲和南美洲的月食。”

Zoe Ortiz is a historian with the University of North Texas.
佐伊·奥尔蒂斯是北德克萨斯大学的历史学家。

She noted that different civilizations have observed lunar eclipses for thousands of years.
她指出，不同文明已经观测月食数千年了。

This helped ancient people learn things about the behaviors of the sun, moon, and stars.
这帮助古人了解了太阳、月球和恒星的行为。

"They were looking at the night sky and they had a much brighter vision than we do today," Ortiz said.
“他们仰望夜空，看到的景象比我们今天要明亮得多，”奥尔蒂斯说。

The ancient Greek thinker and writer Aristotle observed that Earths' shadow on the moon during a lunar eclipse was always curved.
古希腊思想家、作家亚里士多德观察到，月食期间地球在月球上的阴影总是弯曲的。

This fact supported proof that the Earth is round.
这一事实支持了地球是球形的证据。

Read full transcript →

item.title: How Daylight Savings Time Affects Health
item.description: VOA Learning English - How Daylight Savings Time Affects Health. Much of the United States "springs forward" on Sunday, March 9th, for daylight saving time. Worldwide, many other countries also observe daylight saving time, starting and ending on different dates. ... English original and Chinese translation in full notes.
item.content:encoded:
English & 中文

Much of the United States "springs forward" on Sunday, March 9th, for daylight saving time.
美国大部分地区将于3月9日周日“提前”进入夏令时。

Worldwide, many other countries also observe daylight saving time, starting and ending on different dates.
在全球范围内，许多其他国家也实行夏令时，但开始和结束的日期各不相同。

The time change can leave people tired and perhaps unhappy the next day.
时间变化可能会让人第二天感到疲倦，甚至可能心情不佳。

But it also might even harm health.
但它甚至可能对健康有害。

Some studies have found an increase in heart attacks and strokes right after the March time change.
一些研究发现，在3月时间变化后，心脏病发作和中风的数量有所增加。

However, there are ways to ease the effects of the time change, including getting more sunshine.
不过，有一些方法可以减轻时间变化的影响，包括多晒太阳。

The light helps reset your circadian rhythm for healthful sleep.
光线有助于重新调整你的昼夜节律，实现健康睡眠。

In the U.S., daylight saving time begins Sunday at 2:00 in the morning.
在美国，夏令时于周日凌晨2:00开始。

The time change will reverse on November 2 when clocks "fall back" as daylight saving time ends.
时间变化将于11月2日逆转，届时夏令时结束，时钟“回拨”。

The state of Hawaii and most of the state of Arizona do not make the spring change.
夏威夷州和亚利桑那州的大部分地区不实行春季时间调整。

Those areas remain on standard time along with Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
这些地区与波多黎各、美属萨摩亚、关岛和美属维尔京群岛一样，保持标准时间。

Some people try to prepare for the change to daylight saving time by going to bed a little earlier two or three nights ahead.
有些人试图通过提前两三天晚上早睡来为夏令时变化做准备。

But with a third of American adults already not getting the suggested seven hours of nightly sleep, catching up can be difficult.
但由于已有三分之一的美国成年人无法达到建议的每晚七小时睡眠，补觉可能很困难。

The brain has a kind of clock that is set by exposure to sunlight and darkness.
大脑有一种时钟，由暴露在日光和黑暗中设定。

This clock, known as the circadian rhythm, is on a roughly 24-hour cycle.
这个时钟，即昼夜节律，大约以24小时为一个周期。

It governs when we become sleepy and when we are more wakeful.
它控制着我们何时感到困倦，何时更加清醒。

The rhythms change with age.
节律会随着年龄变化。

This is one reason that early-to-rise young children turn into hard-to-wake teenagers.
这就是为什么早睡早起的小孩会变成难叫醒的青少年原因之一。

Morning light resets the rhythm.
晨光可以重置节律。

By evening, levels of a hormone called melatonin begin to increase, leading to tiredness.
到了晚上，一种叫做褪黑素的激素水平开始上升，导致困倦。

Too much light in the evening - that extra hour from daylight saving time - delays the melatonin increase.
晚上光线过多——夏令时多出的那一小时——会延迟褪黑素的增加。

As a result, the cycle gets delayed.
结果，周期被推迟了。

The circadian rhythm affects more than sleep.
昼夜节律影响的不只是睡眠。

It also influences heart rate, blood pressure, hormone releases and other systems.
它还影响心率、血压、激素释放和其他系统。

Sleep deprivation, or lack of sleep, is linked to heart disease, weight conditions, problems with thinking and remembering, and more.
睡眠不足或缺乏睡眠与心脏病、体重问题、思维和记忆障碍等有关。

Deadly car crash numbers increase the first few days after the spring time change, a study of U.S. traffic deaths says.
一项对美国交通死亡人数的研究显示，春季时间变化后的头几天，致命车祸数量增加。

The risk of crashes is highest in the morning, it found.
研究发现，车祸风险在早晨最高。

Read full transcript →

item.title: A Short History of Spacecraft Landings on the Moon
item.description: VOA Learning English - A Short History of Spacecraft Landings on the Moon. Many years have passed since the first spacecraft landed on the moon in 1966. From then until now, there have been many additional attempts with some succeeding and others failing. Here is a short h... English original and Chinese translation in full notes.
item.content:encoded:
English & 中文

Many years have passed since the first spacecraft landed on the moon in 1966.
自1966年第一艘航天器登陆月球以来，许多年过去了。

From then until now, there have been many additional attempts with some succeeding and others failing.
从那时到现在，又进行了多次尝试，有的成功，有的失败。

Here is a short history of some of these attempts.
以下是其中一些尝试的简短历史。

The Soviet Union's Luna 9 spacecraft was the first to land on the moon.
苏联的月球9号航天器是第一个登陆月球的。

It touched down on the lunar surface in 1966.
它于1966年降落在月球表面。

The landing came after several other Soviet spacecraft either did not reach the moon or crashed on the surface.
这次登陆之前，其他几艘苏联航天器要么未能到达月球，要么坠毁在月球表面。

The American space agency NASA says Luna 9 was the first spacecraft to carry out a soft landing on the moon.
美国航天局NASA表示，月球9号是第一个在月球上实现软着陆的航天器。

It was also the first to send "photographic data" from the moon's surface to Earth.
它也是第一个将月球表面的“摄影数据”传回地球的航天器。

Luna 9's landing proved "the lunar surface could support the weight of a lander and that an object would not sink into a loose layer of dust as some models predicted," NASA said.
NASA称，月球9号的着陆证明“月球表面能够承受着陆器的重量，并且物体不会像某些模型预测的那样陷入松散的尘埃层”。

In May 1966, the United States followed with its Surveyor 1 mission.
1966年5月，美国紧随其后执行了勘测者1号任务。

NASA describes this effort as "the first of a series of seven robotic spacecraft sent to the moon to gather data in preparation for NASA's Apollo missions."
NASA将这次任务描述为“为准备NASA阿波罗任务而发送到月球收集数据的七架机器人航天器系列中的第一架”。

The successful soft landing of Surveyor 1 "was one of the great successes of NASA's early lunar and interplanetary program."
勘测者1号的成功软着陆“是NASA早期月球和行星际计划中的重大成功之一”。

Both the U.S. and Soviet Union had other successful robotic landings.
美国和苏联都曾实现过其他成功的机器人着陆。

Next, the countries aimed to be the first to land humans on the moon.
接下来，两国都力争成为第一个将人类送上月球的国家。

In 1969, NASA successfully landed Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the moon.
1969年，NASA成功将阿波罗11号宇航员尼尔·阿姆斯特朗和巴兹·奥尔德林送上月球。

The U.S. Apollo program sent 12 astronauts to explore the moon over six missions.
美国的阿波罗计划通过六次任务共派遣了12名宇航员探索月球。

Apollo 17 was the last in 1972.
阿波罗17号是1972年的最后一次任务。

The U.S. is still the only country to land humans on the moon.
美国仍然是唯一一个将人类送上月球的国家。

NASA officials say the agency's Artemis program aims to return astronauts to the lunar surface possibly by the end of 2026.
NASA官员表示，该机构的阿尔忒弥斯计划目标是在2026年底前将宇航员送回月球表面。

In 2013, China became the third country to successfully land a spacecraft on the moon.
2013年，中国成为第三个成功将航天器送上月球的国家。

China landed an exploring vehicle, or rover named Yutu that year.
同年，中国投放了一辆名为“玉兔”的探测车（即月球车）。

China followed with the Yutu-2 rover in 2019, this time touching down on the moon's unexplored far side.
2019年，中国又发射了玉兔二号月球车，此次降落在月球未被探索的背面。

In 2020, China successfully returned samples of rock and dirt collected by the rovers.
2020年，中国成功将月球车采集的岩石和土壤样本带回地球。

The mission returned about 1.7 kilograms of lunar material collected from the near side of the moon.
该任务带回了约1.7公斤从月球正面收集的月球物质。

Read full transcript →

item.title: Wilbur and Orville Wright: The First Airplane
item.description: VOA Learning English - Wilbur and Orville Wright: The First Airplane. Wilbur and Orville Wright are the American inventors who made a small engine-powered flying machine. They proved that flight without the aid of gas-filled balloons was possible. Wilbur Wright was bo... English original and Chinese translation in full notes.
item.content:encoded:
English & 中文

Wilbur and Orville Wright are the American inventors who made a small engine-powered flying machine.
威尔伯·莱特和奥维尔·莱特是发明了小型发动机驱动飞行器的美国发明家。

They proved that flight without the aid of gas-filled balloons was possible.
他们证明了无需充气气球就能实现飞行。

Wilbur Wright was born in 1867 near Melville, Indiana.
威尔伯·莱特于1867年出生在印第安纳州梅尔维尔附近。

His brother Orville was born four years later in Dayton, Ohio.
他的弟弟奥维尔四年后出生在俄亥俄州代顿市。

As they grew up, the Wright brothers experimented with mechanical things.
成长过程中，莱特兄弟对机械装置进行了各种实验。

Later, the Wright brothers began to design their own flying machine.
后来，莱特兄弟开始设计自己的飞行器。

They used ideas they had developed from earlier experiments with a toy helicopter, kites, the printing machine and bicycles.
他们利用了早期从玩具直升机、风筝、印刷机和自行车实验中得出的想法。

Soon, they needed a place to test their ideas about flight.
很快，他们需要一个地方来测试关于飞行的想法。

The best place with the best wind conditions seemed to be a piece of sandy land in North Carolina along the coast of the Atlantic Ocean.
风况最好的地方似乎是北卡罗来纳州大西洋沿岸的一片沙地。

It was called Kill Devil Hill, near the town of Kitty Hawk.
那里被称为 Kill Devil Hill，靠近基蒂霍克镇。

The Wright brothers did many tests with gliders at Kitty Hawk.
莱特兄弟在基蒂霍克用滑翔机进行了多次测试。

With these tests, they learned how to solve many problems.
通过这些测试，他们学会了如何解决许多问题。

By the autumn of 1903, Wilbur and Orville had designed and built an airplane powered by a gasoline engine.
到1903年秋天，威尔伯和奥维尔已经设计并制造了一架由汽油发动机驱动的飞机。

The plane had wings 12 meters across.
这架飞机的翼展为12米。

It weighed about 340 kilograms, including the pilot.
包括飞行员在内，它重约340公斤。

On December 17th, 1903, they made the world's first flight in a machine that was heavier than air and powered by an engine.
1903年12月17日，他们完成了世界上首次重于空气且由发动机驱动的飞行。

Orville flew the plane 36 meters.
奥维尔驾驶飞机飞行了36米。

He was in the air for 12 seconds.
他在空中停留了12秒。

The two brothers made three more flights that day.
兄弟俩那天又进行了三次飞行。

Four other men watched the Wright brothers' first flights.
有四个人观看了莱特兄弟的首次飞行。

One of the men took pictures.
其中一人拍了照片。

Few newspapers, however, noted the event.
然而，很少有报纸报道这一事件。

It was almost five years before the Wright brothers became famous.
将近五年后，莱特兄弟才出名。

In 1908, Wilbur went to France. He gave demonstration flights at heights of 90 meters.
1908年，威尔伯去了法国。他在90米的高度进行了演示飞行。

A French company agreed to begin making the Wright brothers' flying machine.
一家法国公司同意开始生产莱特兄弟的飞行器。

Orville made successful flights in the United States at the time Wilbur was in France.
在威尔伯在法国期间，奥维尔在美国成功完成了飞行。

The United States War Department agreed to buy a Wright brothers' plane.
美国战争部同意购买一架莱特兄弟的飞机。

Wilbur and Orville suddenly became world heroes.
威尔伯和奥维尔突然成了世界英雄。

But the brothers were not seeking fame.
但兄弟俩并不追求名声。

They returned to Dayton where they continued to improve their airplanes.
他们回到代顿，继续改进他们的飞机。

They taught many others how to fly.
他们教了很多人如何飞行。

Wilbur Wright died of typhoid fever in 1912.
威尔伯·莱特于1912年因伤寒去世。

Read full transcript →
